consolename: Application name displayed in the page header and browser title. IABot is the short name of InternetArchiveBot; translate “Management Interface” as the web application used to control and inspect the bot.
selectwiki: Heading in the account menu for choosing which wiki the tools will operate on. This selects a website, independently of the interface language.
selectlang: Heading in the account menu for choosing the language of this web interface. This does not select the wiki the bot will edit.
activeusers5text: Footer label for the number of people who have used this web interface in the preceding five minutes. “Active” refers to interface activity, not wiki edit counts.

startpagelabel: Name of the interface home page, used in the browser title and navigation. This is the starting page of the application.
runbotmenutitle: Navigation-menu heading grouping tools that run InternetArchiveBot or analyze wiki pages. “Run” means start the software, not run physically.
runbotmenutitlesingle: Menu link to the tool that checks and repairs links on one wiki page using the signed-in user's account.
runbotmenutitlequeuerequest: Menu link to submit a list of wiki pages as a queued bot job. The job is processed later by InternetArchiveBot.
runbotmenutitleanalysis: Menu link to inspect a wiki page's links without saving an edit to that page.
manageurlmenutitle: Navigation-menu heading for editing the bot's stored information about URLs and domains. These tools change database records rather than directly editing a wiki page.
manageurlmenutitlesingle: Menu link to look up and change the bot's stored status and archive information for individual URLs.
manageurlmenutitledomain: Menu link to manage settings that apply to all URLs on an Internet domain, such as a paywall or archive policy.
bugreportmenutitle: Navigation-menu heading grouping ways to report incorrect bot behavior.
bugreportmenutitlefalsepositive: Menu link to report a working URL that the bot incorrectly considers dead. “False positive” specifically means an incorrect dead-link result here.
bugreportmenutitlerealbug: Menu link for reporting software problems other than incorrect dead-link classifications.
metamenutitle: Navigation-menu heading for information and administration of this interface. “Meta” means information about the application, not a link to Meta-Wiki.
metamenutitlelogs: Menu link to the public log of actions performed through this web interface.
metamenutitleusers: Menu link to search accounts that have used this interface.
metamenutitleinfo: Menu link to information about the application's libraries, user groups, permissions, and contributors.
metamenutitlerootheader: Heading separating administrative menu items reserved for users with the highest interface privileges. “Root” means superuser access; it does not refer to Android, a tree, or the root page of a website.
metamenutitlefalsepositivereview: Administrative menu link to review reports of working URLs incorrectly marked dead.
metamenutitlebotqueue: Administrative menu link to inspect and control queued bot jobs, including suspending, resuming, and stopping them.
metamenutitleperformancemetrics: Administrative menu link to measurements of the bot's operation and performance.
metamenutitlestats: Menu link to aggregate statistics about the bot's link processing and edits.

maineditsummary: Configuration-field label for the edit summary attached to the bot's main article edit. An edit summary is the short explanation stored in wiki revision history, distinct from article text or a talk-page message.
maineditsummaryplaceholder:
Hint identifying the configurable summary for the main article edit. This help text is not the summary itself. The field accepts bot counter placeholders and optional conditional clauses; see the syntax notes below.

This is configuration help for translators, not a request to change the wiki's current summary. Administrators opt into detailed summaries in this field; existing configured summaries continue to work. These five optional counters describe main-article changes, not talk-only suggestions or Wikidata's separate edit logic:
* <nowiki>{deadlinksrescued}</nowiki>: first archive added for a source classified as dead.
* <nowiki>{livelinksarchived}</nowiki>: first archive added for a source not classified as dead. This does not guarantee that the source was independently confirmed alive.
* <nowiki>{archivesreplaced}</nowiki>: existing archive links replaced.
* <nowiki>{archivesrepaired}</nowiki>: existing archives whose markup/usage was repaired or normalized.
* <nowiki>{deadtagsremoved}</nowiki>: obsolete dead-link tags removed.

Legacy counters include <nowiki>{linksrescued}</nowiki> (the broader rescue total), <nowiki>{linkstagged}</nowiki> (unfixable dead sources newly marked dead), <nowiki>{linksmodified}</nowiki> (rescued plus tagged), <nowiki>{linksanalyzed}</nowiki> (links examined), and <nowiki>{linksarchived}</nowiki> (successful submissions to the Wayback Machine, not archive-link insertions).

An optional clause has the form <nowiki>{ifany:countername:text}</nowiki>. Its text is included only when the named counter is greater than zero; otherwise the entire clause is omitted. For example, <nowiki>{ifany:deadlinksrescued:Rescued {deadlinksrescued} dead sources.}</nowiki>. Translate the readable clause text, but keep ifany, counter names, braces, and separator colons unchanged. Put punctuation/separating spaces inside a clause when they should disappear with it. Single-brace configuration tokens are different from the interface's double-brace substitutions.

Displayed numbers may use localized digits; conditional clauses still test the underlying numeric counts. The syntax does not choose grammatical singular/plural forms automatically, and MediaWiki PLURAL/GENDER constructs are not evaluated by this interface. Use wording that works with the counts. Only translate the help itself here; translating this message does not alter any saved wiki configuration. An opted-in conditional summary that evaluates to blank uses the existing rescue/tagging fallback rather than saving an empty explanation.
